purpose: Daptomycin is a strong antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial skin infections and bloodstream infections caused by certain bacteria, including MRSA (a tough, drug-resistant staph infection). It is given when other antibiotics may not work well enough. Your doctor may also use it to treat infections of the heart valves caused by Staph bacteria.
how_it_works: Daptomycin works by attaching itself to the outer layer (membrane) of harmful bacteria and punching holes in it. This causes important minerals to leak out of the bacteria, which stops them from making energy and kills them. Think of it like popping a balloon — once the membrane is damaged, the bacteria cannot survive.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, constipation, headache, dizziness, trouble sleeping, rash, and pain or redness at the injection site. Some patients may notice muscle pain or weakness, so let your doctor or pharmacist know right away if your muscles feel unusually sore.
warnings: Important: Daptomycin can sometimes cause muscle breakdown, a serious condition called myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Your doctor will check your blood for muscle enzymes (called CPK levels) during treatment. Tell your doctor immediately if you have severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine. Also, do NOT take daptomycin for lung infections — it does not work well in the lungs. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially cholesterol-lowering drugs called statins, as combining them may increase muscle risk.
typical_dosing: Daptomycin is given as an IV (intravenous) infusion directly into your vein — you cannot take it as a pill. For skin infections, the usual dose is 4 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given once daily over 30 minutes. For bloodstream or heart infections, the dose is higher, usually 6 mg per kg once daily. Your doctor will adjust the dose if your kidneys are not working at full strength.
